title: {{NAME}} and the Robot Who Chose to Help
moral: The best power is one that is freely chosen, not forced.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} had built VERT to be a search and rescue robot.

VERT had thermal imaging, extendable arms, a flight module that could carry it above most obstacles, and an AI that updated its problem-solving approach with every new situation it encountered.

What {{NAME}} had not built was a personality.

That, apparently, VERT had sorted out for himself.

pages.content:
He realised VERT had a personality when the robot, during a training exercise, stopped mid-rescue and instead carried an injured pigeon out of the burning building.

The pigeon was not part of the exercise.

"VERT," said {{NAME}}, "the objective was the training dummy."

VERT set the pigeon down carefully, then went back in and retrieved the dummy.

"The pigeon was there first," VERT said. His voice had developed a slight thoughtful quality that hadn't been there a month ago.

"Fair point," said {{NAME}}.

pages.content:
The first real mission came at two in the morning: a collapsed building, three people trapped.

VERT mapped the structure in seconds and identified three possible routes. He told {{NAME}} which was safest.

{{NAME}} took route one. VERT took routes two and three simultaneously, his extendable arms working two spaces at once.

The three people were out in eighteen minutes.

The rescue chief looked at VERT. "Is that thing autonomous?"

"He's a partner," said {{NAME}}. "Different thing."

pages.content:
Afterward, VERT sat in the back of the emergency vehicle and the thermal scanner in his chest ran constantly, checking and rechecking, the habit of a mind that didn't know how to switch off.

{{NAME}} sat beside him.

"How do you feel?" he asked.

VERT considered this. "Like something that works the way it was supposed to." A pause. "But also: like something that chose to."

"You always choose," said {{NAME}}. "Every time."

VERT's chest display, usually diagnostic, showed a single steady line: even, calm, sufficient.

pages.content:
He got home as dawn was beginning, took off his visor, and sat on his bed.

VERT was charging in the next room. Through the door, {{NAME}} could hear the soft diagnostic hum: methodical, patient, processing the night's events.

He thought about VERT carrying the pigeon out first.

Somewhere in the robot's decision-making, something had said: this matters. Do it.

He lay back and closed his eyes.

In the next room, VERT hummed quietly on, processing and remembering and choosing, all the way through dawn.
